The correct answer is: neutrophils'), but this is pathologically wrong -- Langhans giant cells form from the fusion of activated epithelioid macrophages, not neutrophils, a fact this same lecture's own Q3/Q5 rows (macrophage as the key granuloma cell; epithelioid cells as modified macrophages) directly contradict. questions.title: Endarteritis obliterans means thick-walled arteries with narrow lumen
questions.question: Endarteritis obliterans means:

explanations.A: Incorrect. This is the opposite finding -- endarteritis obliterans thickens the vessel wall and narrows the lumen, it does not thin the wall or widen the lumen.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Being an end artery is an unrelated anatomical fact about a vessel's supply pattern, not a description of the chronic intimal thickening that defines endarteritis obliterans.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Endarteritis obliterans narrows the lumen through wall thickening; describing it as complete obliteration overstates the process, which is progressive narrowing, not necessarily total closure.
explanations.D: Correct. Endarteritis obliterans is chronic thickening of the arterial intima. The vessel wall becomes thicker while its lumen narrows, producing the classic thick-walled, narrow-lumen picture. It is seen accompanying chronic granulomatous and chronic infective processes such as tuberculosis.

questions.learning_objective: State that endarteritis obliterans means thick-walled arteries with a narrowed lumen, from chronic intimal thickening.

questions.title: Macrophage is the most important cell in granuloma development
questions.question: The most important cell in the development of a granuloma is a:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neutrophils are the hallmark cell of acute, not granulomatous, inflammation -- they are not the driving cell of a granuloma.
explanations.B: Correct. The macrophage, transformed by persistent antigenic stimulation into an epithelioid cell, is the central, key cell of every granuloma. Activated macrophages present antigen, respond to T-cell lymphokines, and can fuse into giant cells, making them the cell type that both forms and defines the granuloma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mast cells drive immediate (type I) hypersensitivity reactions, not the type IV, macrophage-driven process that builds a granuloma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Fibroblasts contribute to the later fibrotic/healing response around a chronic lesion, not to the granuloma's defining epithelioid-macrophage architecture.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the (epithelioid) macrophage as the central cell of granuloma formation.

questions.title: Giant cells accompany a leaking silicone breast implant
questions.question: Which of the following cell types would be most characteristic of the inflammatory response accompanying a leaking silicone breast implant:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mast cells characterise immediate hypersensitivity reactions, not the foreign-body granulomatous response to an indigestible material like leaked silicone.
explanations.B: Correct. Leaked silicone is an indigestible foreign material. Macrophages that cannot break it down fuse into multinucleated foreign-body giant cells around it, making the giant cell the most characteristic accompanying inflammatory cell in this setting.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Neutrophils dominate acute, pus-forming inflammation, not the chronic granulomatous reaction that surrounds a retained foreign material such as silicone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Plasma cells are a chronic-inflammation cell type but are not the characteristic, defining cell of a foreign-body reaction the way the giant cell is.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Eosinophils mark parasitic infection or allergic/immediate hypersensitivity reactions, not a foreign-body giant-cell reaction to inert silicone.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise a foreign-body giant-cell reaction from a leaking silicone implant vignette.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Giant cell"

questions.title: Silicosis is a cause of non-infective granuloma
questions.question: Which of the following is a cause of non infective granuloma:

explanations.A: Correct. Silicosis, from chronic inhalation of crystalline silica particles that macrophages cannot digest, is a standard non-infective cause of granuloma -- the trigger is an inert particle, not an organism. The particles resist macrophage digestion the same way an indigestible foreign material does, sustaining the same persistent-antigen-style stimulus that drives epithelioid-macrophage transformation. This inert-particle mechanism is what separates silicosis from every infective cause on this list.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bilharziasis is caused by Schistosoma ova and is an infective, not non-infective, cause of granulomatous inflammation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is a classic infective cause of granuloma, not a non-infective one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae and, like tuberculosis, is an infective granuloma-forming disease.

questions.learning_objective: Classify silicosis as a non-infective cause of granuloma, distinct from tuberculosis, bilharziasis and leprosy.

questions.title: Epithelioid cells are modified macrophages
questions.question: Epithelioid cells are modiﬁed:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lymphocytes are present in a granuloma and drive macrophage activation through lymphokines, but they are not themselves what transforms into an epithelioid cell.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Despite the name, epithelioid cells are not derived from epithelial cells -- "epithelioid" describes their epithelium-like microscopic appearance, not their cell of origin.
explanations.C: Correct. Epithelioid cells are macrophages that have been transformed by persistent antigenic stimulation. They enlarge, flatten their nucleus and gain abundant pink cytoplasm that resembles epithelium, which is where the name "epithelioid" comes from. Despite that epithelium-like appearance, they remain macrophages in origin and function, and are the key cell of granuloma formation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Plasma cells are antibody-secreting B-lymphocyte derivatives found in chronic inflammation, not the cell that transforms into an epithelioid cell.

questions.learning_objective: State that epithelioid cells are macrophages transformed by persistent antigenic stimulation.

questions.title: Ghon's focus is a tuberculous reaction
questions.question: Ghon's focus consists of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A foreign-body reaction forms around an indigestible material such as suture or silicone, not around Mycobacterium tuberculosis at the site of primary infection.
explanations.B: Correct. The Ghon focus is the small, typically subpleural, lesion of primary tuberculosis infection in the lung. It is a tuberculous granulomatous reaction, built from the same epithelioid-macrophage response as any other tuberculous lesion. Together with draining hilar lymph node involvement it forms the primary (Ghon) complex, the hallmark of primary pulmonary tuberculosis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Non-specific inflammatory reaction" is too generic -- the Ghon focus has a specific, tuberculous granulomatous cause, not an undifferentiated inflammatory one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A bilharzial reaction is caused by Schistosoma ova, an entirely different infective process from the Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection that produces the Ghon focus.

questions.learning_objective: State that the Ghon focus is a tuberculous reaction, the lesion of primary tuberculosis infection.

questions.title: Lymphokines mediate the chronic inflammation of delayed hypersensitivity
questions.question: The chronic inﬂammation of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction is mediated by

explanations.A: Incorrect. Complement acts chiefly in acute inflammation and antibody-mediated (type II/III) hypersensitivity, not in the T-cell-driven chronic inflammation of a delayed (type IV) reaction.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bradykinin is a mediator of acute inflammation's vascular changes and pain, not of the lymphocyte-driven chronic inflammation of delayed hypersensitivity.
explanations.C: Correct. Lymphokines are cytokines released by activated T lymphocytes. They recruit and activate macrophages at the reaction site, sustaining the mononuclear infiltrate. This lymphokine-driven activation is what mediates the chronic inflammation of a delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity reaction, including granuloma formation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Histamine is the principal mediator of immediate (type I) hypersensitivity and early acute-inflammatory vasodilation, not of delayed hypersensitivity's chronic inflammation.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Polymorphs (neutrophils) are a cell type, not a chemical mediator, and they characterise acute rather than chronic inflammation.

questions.learning_objective: State that lymphokines mediate the chronic inflammation of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction.
